pdf.inspectionSummary: This inspection identified a total of {{count}} damage(s) across all three blades of turbine {{turbineName}}.
pdf.generalInformationDescription: This methodology is classified as a visual remote inspection using cameras, an access method expressly permitted and contemplated within the scope of periodic inspections of the DNVGL-ST-0376 standard.
pdf.technologyDescription: The inspection was carried out via drone access, capturing high-resolution photographs. This methodology complies with the remote visual inspection guidelines established in the applicable standard DNV GL-ST-0376. For this purpose, the company used the DJI Matrice 4E model as its primary equipment, equipped with a 4/3" CMOS sensor, 20 MP, variable aperture (f/2.8 - f/11), and a mechanical shutter. This methodology aligns with the requirements of the aforementioned standard, which contemplates and permits remote visual inspection using cameras. To meet the technical quality criteria in the inspection, the determining factor is not a fixed distance, but achieving an optimal level of detail. Our methodology ensures a minimum resolution of 1 pixel/mm for a correct evaluation of damages. Consequently, the flight distance was adapted to the sensor's capacity to guarantee the required sharpness while maintaining operational safety.
pdf.confidentialityText: All information contained in this inspection report is strictly confidential. Its content has been prepared solely for internal purposes authorized by VND Blade Platform and its affiliated entities. Any unauthorized reproduction, distribution, or disclosure, in whole or in part, is strictly prohibited without prior written consent from the company.
pdf.cat1Action: No action necessary, continue operation, monitor at next inspection.
pdf.cat2Description: Minor. No impact to the functional integrity of the blade.
pdf.cat2Action: No action necessary, monitor at next inspection.
pdf.cat3Description: Functional, minor impact to the functional integrity of the blade
pdf.cat3Action: Operate normally, but plan minor repair at the next scheduled shutdown.
pdf.cat4Description: Serious Damage, impact on the functional or structural integrity of the blade
pdf.cat4Action: Reduce load if possible and schedule preventive shutdown in 1-2 months for repair.
pdf.cat5Description: Critical Damage. Structural integrity severely compromised
pdf.cat5Action: Immediate turbine shutdown. Do not restart until evaluation and repair are complete.
pdf.dateAndWTGText: On {{inspectionDate}} an external blade inspection was carried out on wind turbine {{turbineName}} part of the {{windFarm}} project owned by {{client}}.
pdf.targetText: The objective of this inspection report is to provide an overview of the external physical condition of all blades (Blade A, Blade B, and Blade C) on turbine {{turbineName}}, thereby enabling follow-up and prompt attention to the identified damages. Total damages found: {{totalDamages}}.
pdf.defBladeRoot: A specific point on the longitudinal axis of the blade measured from the exact center of the hub.
pdf.defLeadingEdge: The leading edge of the blade, i.e. the 'nose' that is heading into the wind during operation.
pdf.defSuctionSide: The side of the blade which faces the tower during turbine operation.
pdf.defShell: The function of the shell is to give an aerodynamic profile.
pdf.defSpar: The structural part of the blade positioned between the shells.
pdf.defTrailingEdge: The thin edge where the airflow leaves the blade during operation.
pdf.defPressureSide: The side facing the wind, also known as the High pressure side.
pdf.defSMT: Solid Metal Tip, part of lightning protection system.
pdf.defCore: Material between the two layers of laminate, typically foam or balsa.
pdf.defLPS: Lightning Protection System designed to protect from lightning strikes.
pdf.projectOverviewText: This report presents the results of the drone inspection carried out on wind turbine {{turbineName}} at {{windFarm}} wind park, part of the {{projectName}} project. The inspection was conducted on {{inspectionDate}} using advanced aerial inspection technology.
pdf.immediateAction: IMMEDIATE ACTION: Critical damages (Cat 5) detected. Requires urgent intervention.
pdf.highPriority: HIGH PRIORITY: Severe damages (Cat 4) require short-term maintenance planning.
pdf.mediumPriority: MEDIUM PRIORITY: Monitor moderate damages (Cat 3) to prevent progression.
pdf.excellentCondition: The wind turbine is in excellent condition with no damages detected.
pdf.continueInspections: Continue with regular inspections for preventive monitoring.
pdf.reviewDetailedReport: Review the detailed report for specific actions per damage.
pdf.dnvReference1: An external visual inspection was carried out. As a normative reference, the DNV-GL-ST-0376 standard recommends conducting a comprehensive blade assessment covering the following points:
pdf.dnvReference2: Planning of internal inspections as well as the inspection of components in the LPS system to consider the following points and rule out anomalies and/or damages that are not visible through this external inspection:
pdf.dnvBullet1: • Structural integrity of the laminates, on both the outer and inner surfaces.
pdf.dnvBullet2: • Condition of the adhesive joints at the leading and trailing edges.
pdf.dnvBullet3: • Internal adhesive joints, such as the shear web joints.
pdf.dnvBullet6: • Corrosion and pre-tension level in the bolts.
